programs.nl_rule: The input contains red rectangles and single-marker blue cells placed along the outer edges of the grid. When a blue cell is placed on one edge of the grid, there is also a blue cell at the corresponding position on the opposite edge. The output grid size stays the same.  Connect blue cells on opposite edges. Connect left and right cells with a horizontal blue line, and top and bottom cells with a vertical blue line. Any red rectangle crossed by one of these lines becomes blue. Everything else stays unchanged.

Ah! Markers on the top-left corner are on BOTH the top edge and left edge. So (0,0) adds both h_line 0 and v_line 0. Similarly (0,6) is top and right edge -> v_line 6 and h_line 0.

So in demo3, v_lines={0,6}, h_lines={0}. So the line col0 and col6 become 1, plus row0. And rect rows3-4 cols1-2: is it adjacent to v_line col0? col1 neighbor col0 -> line -> hit! So rect converts to blue. That explains output.

Also output row0 all 1, col0 all 1, col6 all 1. And rows3-4 cols1-2 blue.

OK so corner markers create both lines. Good to know. My demo4: markers at (1,0),(1,6) -> left/right edge -> h_line row1. No top/bottom. Rect rows2-3 cols1-3 adjacent to row1 -> blue. Output matches.

But wait, also v_lines might include... no. Rect Q cols2-4 rows1-3 contains col3 -> blue. P untouched.
